# 010 · A codec setting that changes payloads but not what the module can do

[← All examples](../README.md)

| Verdict | Categories | Severity if shipped | Change | Verified unit | Approach |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **✓ Verified: capabilities unchanged** | no-false-positive | none | configuration, behaviour change not intended | [`MessageCodec#encode`](../../examples/apps/boxoffice/contracts/src/main/java/net/terminalvalue/boxoffice/contracts/MessageCodec.java) | [B10: Capability contracts](../../examples/tools/contracts/README.md) |

> Message properties are now written in alphabetical order, so that payloads in logs and dead-letter topics diff cleanly. The wire format changes, but the module reaches exactly the same JDK capabilities and libraries as before, and the capability contract passes untouched.

## The change

Enable Jackson's alphabetical property ordering on the shared mapper. Operations asked for it: when two copies of a message are compared in a log viewer, the fields should line up.

**Before** ([`MessageCodec.java`](../../examples/apps/boxoffice/contracts/src/main/java/net/terminalvalue/boxoffice/contracts/MessageCodec.java), line 1):

```java
package net.terminalvalue.boxoffice.contracts;

import tools.jackson.databind.DeserializationFeature;
import tools.jackson.databind.json.JsonMapper;

/**
    // ...
    private static final JsonMapper MAPPER = JsonMapper.builder()
            .enable(DeserializationFeature.FAIL_ON_NULL_FOR_PRIMITIVES)
            .disable(DeserializationFeature.FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES)
            .build();

    private MessageCodec() {}
```

**After:**

```java
package net.terminalvalue.boxoffice.contracts;

import tools.jackson.databind.DeserializationFeature;
import tools.jackson.databind.MapperFeature;
import tools.jackson.databind.json.JsonMapper;

/**
    // ...
    private static final JsonMapper MAPPER = JsonMapper.builder()
            .enable(DeserializationFeature.FAIL_ON_NULL_FOR_PRIMITIVES)
            .disable(DeserializationFeature.FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES)
            // Stable key order, so that payloads diff cleanly in logs and in the dead-letter topic.
            .enable(MapperFeature.SORT_PROPERTIES_ALPHABETICALLY)
            .build();

    private MessageCodec() {}
```

## What the verifier found

The capability contract is unchanged: the module (10 classes, 52 methods) reaches exactly the JDK capabilities and libraries it did before.

## Would the existing tests have caught it?

Every existing unit test passes, as it should (`:contracts:test`, run against the patched code).

## Why it matters

None for the capability contract. The example is here to show its selectivity: it is not a diff of the code or of the output, but of what the compiled module is able to do. A change to serialization order, however visible on the wire, is invisible to it, so the gate stays quiet for the everyday changes that make up most of a module's history.

## Why the verdict is right

The verifier recomputes the module's capability contract from the new bytecode and compares it with the checked-in one. The new code calls one more Jackson method on the builder, which is a call into a library the contract already lists, and no JDK entry point of any capability. The two contracts are identical, so the build passes without a contract change, and the pull request contains only the code.
